findings.title: Task 2's "full suite passes unchanged" success criterion is not achievable
findings.description:
Task 2 adds four `SnapshotMetric` members (and three `AbsenceReason` members) and narrows `PythonAdapter.metrics` to the explicit four 400 metrics, then asserts **"Success: the full `tests/metrology/` suite passes unchanged."** That cannot hold. Three tests pin the old 4-metric invariants and will break the moment the enum grows to 8, with no task telling the implementer to edit them:

- `tests/metrology/snapshot/test_python_length.py:57` — `assert adapter.metrics == set(SnapshotMetric)`. After Task 2 the adapter declares 4 but `set(SnapshotMetric)` is 8 → assertion fails.
- `tests/metrology/snapshot/test_render.py` (`python_snapshot`, ~L33–50) — builds a `LanguageSnapshot` with exactly 4 `Measurement`s. `LanguageSnapshot._one_measurement_per_metric` (`src/squadron/metrology/snapshot_models.py`) requires every member of `set(SnapshotMetric)` (now 8) → `ValidationError` at construction.
- `tests/metrology/snapshot/test_snapshot_models.py` (`test_json_round_trip_is_lossless`, ~L213–235) — same 4-metric `LanguageSnapshot` construction → `ValidationError`.

A junior executing Task 2 will see a red suite and have no guidance on which tests encode the pre-extension contract and must be updated (they are not "the 400 length tests adjusted only for the rename"). The task should either drop "passes unchanged," or explicitly name these invariant-pinning tests as expected edits. The downstream incremental additions (Task 8 complexity, 12/14 duplication, 25 coverage) are handled correctly, so this is localized to Task 2's success line.

findings.title: Token-bound performance property is guarded functionally, not by a load test
findings.description: The slice's "linear in tokens, memory ≈133 B/token, `DUPLICATION_MAX_TOKENS = 4_000_000` ceiling" property is verified by Task 11's `monkeypatch`-lowered-constant test (`tool_failed` naming count and ceiling) plus the `MemoryError` test, rather than a `tests/load/` case. That is adequate because the bound is a functional guard the design tests by forcing the threshold, and the slice does not restate a load NFR requiring a `tests/load/` task — so no gap. Noted only to record the decision so it is not mistaken for an oversight.
